newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines allows peso to move in "wider" range.
newsitem.headline: Philippines allows peso to move in "wider" range.

text.p: The Philippines Central Bank said on Friday that it would allow the peso to move in a wider range against the dollar.
"Starting today....(it) will allow the peso-U.S. dollar rate to move within a new wider range consistent with significantly changed market conditions," it said in a statement.

"This is expected to remove the incentive for speculation against the peso and allow a gradual reduction in interest rates more compatible with the economy's requirements for sustainable economic growth," the statement said.
The Bank gave no indication of what the wider rate would be.
"(The Bank) remains fully committed to the market-oriented exchange rate arrangement which has served the Philippines well," it said.

"While the underlying exchange rate policy will remain unchanged, (the Central Bank) will allow greater flexibility in the peso-U.S. dollar rate. This is being taken to facilitate more timely adjustment in light of more difficult conditions in regional currency markets," the statement said.
It added that the move would to done in the context of continued prudent macro-economic policies.
Central Bank, Governor Gabirel Singson is due to give a press conference on Firday at 10 am (0200 gmt).
